https://issues.rudder.io/issues/27147

Enable back `-Werror`. 

I needed to disable some checks: 

- disable safe initiationlization check. There is too much work to do, and that work is hard, long, and not correlated with the switch to scala 3
- remove an existantial warning on `BoxTrait`, because we can't do anything about it, 

And correct two other: 

- `ExecutionBatch`: actually, all `LastRunAvailable` are also `ExpectedConfigAvailable`. That makes little sense for a run with a deleted exepected config, so I'm not sure what happens here, but the encoding say so and scalac3 saw it - there is an `Unexpected` case
- `Query` lexer/parser : there was `lift-json` objects used as intermediary, that we really don't need anymore. Just use direct `zio-json` decoding, simplify everything. Some tests were irrelevant (checking for non empty string while the soundess is done later on)
- some sub-component encoding was relying on uncheck runtime erasure, so I changed it a bit. 

Now, everything compiles without warning :tada: 

Also, I changed `spotless` from `verify` (of very late phase, just before installing) to `validate` (a very early phase, before compilation).

body:
Significant rework of level data generation for the maze generator. Fixed a bunch of bugs in the maze generation algorithm itself (which I think already got pulled into dev), but now the level data generation is much more efficient by only doing math when it needs to. `BP_LevelDataGenerator` demonstrates how the maze generator wants to generate its data for yous now.

In order to facilitate this, I've added a number of hopefully helpful macros.
* For loops in unreal by default start a bunch of loops practically simultaneously and report complete once they've *started*, not when they've *ended* all of those loops. There is now a `ForLoop_Real` macro in the newly created `BPML_Utilities`, which waits for each loop to finish before starting the next loop, but it does require hooking up the end of the loop body to the Continue pin.
* There is also now a `BPML_3dArray` which adds special for loops for looping through grids of 3d points based on IntVectors. there are both real and unreal versions of these loops, and they are explicitely *not* nested for loops, to minimize chances of infinite loop errors. Rather, they map between integer indices and 3d IntVectors within the macro. There's a couple helper macros as well in there.
* I've also copied the flow control macros from `BPML_Math` and the batching macros from `BPML_Utils` into `BPML_Utilities` for better organization. Unfortunately, `BPML_Utils` was made as an actor macro library, meaning its macros can't be used in other types of objects such as actor components. Any files using these macros should be updated to use the ones from `BPML_Utilities` instead, where any further updates will go.

This branch may be pruned when merged.

author: davidanson
body:
@haslinghuis asked me to look at removing this project’s use of jBox. Part 1/2 of that can be found in #4484; this is Part 2/2. However, whereas replacing model dialogs could be done ~without compromise, removing tooltips may not be as clean. First, the good news: - This implementation is a CSS-only approach that leverages much of the existing infrastructure. You'll see the code diff is small and well-contained. No code needs to be run to display tooltips and the DOM is not bloated by extra elements. - The “Configuration” tab is a good place to play around without hitting too many sharp corners. - Because of the use of CSS `hover`, tooltips open immediately (but I do not see this as a problem). Next, some problems with the prototype that can be fixed: - The prototype ALSO displays standard HTML tooltips because of the (existing) use of the “title” attribute. This redundant behavior could be avoided by using a different attribute, but I left it in to show that native HTML tooltips are ALSO an option. However, they cannot be styled at all, and I assumed that was a dealbreaker. But what's nice about native HTML tooltips is that they should be fully accessible and would be even simpler than this diff. They’re not very pretty, but are guaranteed to work everywhere. :) - Line breaks can be used in the proposed CSS tooltip approach (FYI, they work with native HTML tooltips also). I have converted one example: the “?” to the right of the “Choose a Board” message on the “Firmware Flasher" tab. Updating requires replacing `
` with `\n` in about 200 places in the localized strings file, which is easy but not something I wanted to do proactively. - Every CSS tooltip opens to the right because it doesn't know any better. While that’s usually fine, when it happens for elements at the right side of the screen, the tooltip gets clipped. The best way I see to fix this is to use a dedicated CSS class name for the handful of tooltips that need to open left (ex: `cf_tip_left`). This would be a simple, one-time manual change. If we wanted to run some code, maybe each tab could be scanned after initialization and updated at runtime. I didn't want to spend time on this prematurely. - You can see examples where opening left is necessary on the "PID Tuning" tab. Finally, the bad news: - This CSS tooltip approach does not support HTML syntax at all. (And neither do native HTML tooltips.) Styling within tooltips is not used extensively by this project, BUT there are various instances of emphasis and some hyperlinks, all of which would need to be converted to plain text. The “Choose a Board” example above includes one such link at the end. In general, the lack of styling is not a usability catastrophy, but it represents a regression from where things are today. Again, the “Choose a Board” example shows an example of the text “Cloud Build” losing its bold styling. I don't know how big a deal loss of formatting is and I don't see a clean way around it other than moving to a dedicated library for tooltips. But at that point, it's not clear to me why the project wouldn't just stay with jBox which is already implemented and working. There could be size or performance benefits to a different library, but I'm not familiar enough with the landscape to recommend one. I didn't explore this option, but assume something could be found with similar requirements as jBox. So that's the state of things as I understand them. I'd ask interested parties to please play around with this prototype to get sense of what the compromises are. Then let me know what you think! :) Note: The OSD tab has its own call to initialize jBox/Tooltip. It looks similar, so I did not spend time on that tab assuming there won't be any new issues there.

Summary of Changes
This PR fixes critical layout issues in the Smart Notes grid by implementing a proper masonry layout system. The changes resolve double spacing problems, improve responsive column behavior, and ensure cards flow naturally with varying heights while maintaining optimal space utilization across all screen sizes.
Key Changes
This PR addresses layout inconsistencies in the Smart Notes grid that were causing visual spacing issues and poor responsive behavior.
The main improvements include implementing a true masonry layout using CSS columns instead of CSS Grid, which allows cards with different heights to flow naturally like Pinterest-style layouts. The break-inside-avoid property prevents cards from being split across columns, while mb-4 provides consistent vertical spacing between cards. The responsive column system (columns-1 sm:columns-2 lg:columns-3 xl:columns-4 2xl:columns-5) automatically adjusts from 1 column on mobile to 5 columns on large screens, ensuring optimal space utilization. These changes eliminate the double spacing issues that occurred with the previous grid implementation and provide a more visually appealing, scalable layout that adapts seamlessly to different content lengths and screen sizes.

author: kafetzisthomas
body:
### Vulnerabilities Fixed

**HTTP Response Log Injection:**
`request.path` is not escaped in logs allowing attackers to manipulate log output via crafted URLs.

**Denial-of-Service (DoS):**
- `strip_tags()` and `striptags` filter are vulnerable to slow processing of incomplete HTML tags.
- NFKC normalization on Windows causes slowdowns in `LoginView`, `LogoutView`, and `set_language` with large Unicode inputs.
- `wrap()` method and `wordwrap` filter can be exploited with very long strings.

author: veenaramesh
body:
# Fixing app deployment to use Databricks SDK and other minor fixes

## Overview
This PR addresses **10 issues** in LLMOps Stacks by restructuring the Databricks App deployment. Instead of multiple small fixes, this PR uses the Databricks SDK that simplifies deployment and improves DAB integration.

## Issues
### Core changes
1. App Deployment
- **Issue**: Shell scripts (`deploy.sh`, `create.sh`, `sync.sh`) failed within Databricks workflows and couldn't launch the app.
- **Fix**: Replaced shell script approach with Databricks SDK for app creation and deployment.
- **Now**: Creates app link directly in notebook cells. 

2. Consolidated App Configuration
- **Issue**: Multiple configuration files scattered across directories for a single app deployment
- **Fix**: Rewrote `LaunchApp.py` to use `%%writefile` magic commands to generate required files:
  - `DatabricksChatbot.py`
  - `app.py` 
  - `app.yaml`
- **Now**: Single source of truth for app configuration, simplified maintenance

3. Parameterized Deployment Job
- **Issue**: Databricks SDK requires `app_name`, `catalog`, `schema`, and `model_name` but these weren't configurable
- **Fix**: Added parameters to deployment job in resource via widgets for all required inputs

### DAB Integration Improvements

4. App Resource Management
- **Issue**: Databricks App wasn't controlled by DAB, leading to orphaned resources
- **Fix**: Added App resource definition to resource YAML files
- **Now**: Full management through DAB. Validated that `bundle destroy` removes the app and deployment.

5. App Name Configuration
- **Issue**: No mechanism to control app naming through DAB variables
- **Fix**: Added `chatbot_name` variable to `databricks.yaml`

6. Resource File Restructuring
- **Issue**: `ml-artifacts-resource.yaml` name no longer accurate after adding App resources
- **Fix**: Renamed to `agents-artifacts-resource.yaml` to reflect broader scope

### API Integration Fixes
7. Model Querying Implementation
- **Issue**: Databricks SDK queries failing with `IndexError` despite healthy endpoints ([Reference: Previous PR](https://github.com/kevin-hartman/llmops-stacks/pull/3))
- **Fix**: Replaced SDK approach with `mlflow.deployments` client

### File Format Standardization
8. Notebook Format Migration
- **Change**: Converted all Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb`) to Python source files (`.py`)
- **Reason**: Python files are cleaner, more version-control friendly, and recommended for production workflows

9. Resource Reference Updates
- **Issue**: DAB deployment failures due to incorrect file extension references (due to change 8). 
- **Fix**: Updated all workflow resource definitions to reference `.py` files instead of `.ipynb`

10. File Cleanup
- **Issue**: Orphaned `(Clone) AgentEvaluation.py` file with no references
- **Fix**: Removed unused file

## Testing & Validation
- Template completes successfully without errors
- Bundle Validation passes all DAB validation checks  
- All workflows run end-to-end successfully
- Validated on AWS deployment
- GitHub Actions and other CI/CD workflows not yet tested

## Identified limitations

### Bundle Destruction Issues
- `databricks bundle destroy` fails to delete Registered Model (because it is "not empty")

### Unmanaged Resources  
The following resources are created outside DAB and require manual cleanup:
- **Agent Deployment Assets**:
  - Feedback registered model
  - CPU endpoint for agent and feedback model
  - Payload table
- **Data Assets**:
  - Volume with Databricks documentation
  - Delta tables (raw docs, processed docs, evaluation table)
- **Vector Search**:
  - index
  - endpoint
- **UC Functions**:
  - `ask_ai`
  - `execute_python_code`
  - `summarize`
  - `translate`

author: antoinechambert-loir
body:
This file contains elementary definitions involving congruence
relations and morphisms for semirings, rings, and algebras.

* `RingCon.ker`: the kernel of a monoid homomorphism as a congruence relation
* `RingCon.lift`, `RingCon.liftₐ`: the homomorphism / the algebra morphism
  on the quotient given that the congruence is in the kernel
* `RingCon.map`, `RingCon.mapₐ`: homomorphism / algebra morphism
  from a smaller to a larger quotient

* `RingCon.quotientKerEquivRangeS`, `RingCon.quotientKerEquivRange`,
  `RingCon.quotientKerEquivRangeₐ` :
  the first isomorphism theorem for semirings (using `RingHom.rangeS`),
  rings (using `RingHom.range`) and algebras (using `AlgHom.range`).
* `RingCon.comapQuotientEquivRangeS`, `RingCon.comapQuotientEquivRange`,
  `RingCon.comapQuotientEquivRangeₐ` : the second isomorphism theorem
  for semirings (using `RingHom.rangeS`), rings (using `RingHom.range`)
  and algebras (using `AlgHom.range`).

* `RingCon.quotientQuotientEquivQuotient`, `RingCon.quotientQuotientEquivQuotientₐ` :
  the third isomorphism theorem for semirings (or rings) and algebras



It is an adaptation of what existed for multiplicative congruences (docs#Con) and is only useful for semirings which are not rings.

author: rohitrastogi
body:
This PR replaces the existing `semantic.group_by().agg()` functionality with a  more flexible `semantic.with_cluster_labels()` method.

- Replaces `df.semantic.group_by().agg()` with `df.semantic.cluster(by, num_clusters, return_centroids=False)`
- Adds a cluster label column (naming configurable) containing integer cluster assignments (`0` to `num_clusters - 1`)
- Optionally adds a cluster centroid column containing centroid embeddings when `cluster_centroid_column` is not None.
- Enables users to perform standard DataFrame operations such as `group_by("cluster_label")` for custom aggregations, giving them greater control
- Update examples to use the new API.

## Motivation

The previous `semantic.group_by().agg()` pattern was restrictive because it immediately aggregated data. The new method  adds flexibility by adding cluster metadata columns, which users can then leverage with standard DataFrame operations like filtering, grouping, window functions (though session.sql()) and custom aggregations.

## Example Usage

```python
# Basic clustering (replaces semantic.group_by)
clustered_df = df.semantic.with_cluster_labels("feedback_embeddings", 5)

# Use regular operations to analyze clusters
clustered_df.group_by("cluster_label").agg(count("*"), avg("rating"))

# Filter outliers using centroids
clustered_df = df.semantic.cluster("embeddings", 3, centroid_column="cluster_centroid")
clean_df = clustered_df.filter(
    embedding.compute_similarity("embeddings", "cluster_centroid", metric="cosine") > 0.7
)
